title: fix(app-shell): the action editor writes a script body that names its language (objectui#11921)
body:
Fixes #11921

Clause-②: no

Every script body Studio's action inspector writes now names its language. The "What it does: Run a script" switch seeds the body's language, typing keeps it, and a language change writes the new language's shape. The first keystroke into a fresh body parses through the spec's `ActionSchema`. One part of the triage pins cannot be met as written, and this PR does not meet it by inventing content. **After the switch** the body is refused at `body.source` until the author types, because the spec requires a non-empty source in both languages. See "Where the triage pin and the spec disagree" below.

## What changes

All in `packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/inspectors/ActionDefaultInspector.tsx`:

- **One writer, `writeScriptBody`.** `patchBody` (each keystroke, each language pick) and `commitOperation` (the switch to *Run a script*) both write the body through it.
  - It guarantees `language`. A language the body already names is kept as written. Only an absent one is seeded.
  - A language change writes the new language's shape. Keys that only the old language admits are dropped (`capabilities`, `timeoutMs` and `memoryMb` on a switch from JS to an expression). The per-language key sets are a constant in the inspector, `BODY_KEYS_BY_LANGUAGE`. A parity pin in the test file compares it with `HookBodySchema.options` in both directions, importing the spec on the test side only, so the schema stays out of the console's first load. (The first round read the keys off the spec at runtime, which kept 7 spec declarations, about +0.6 KB gzip, in the eager closure.) A key that neither language admits is kept, so the spec's refusal can name it to the author.
  - `source` is never seeded.
- **The seeded language is `expression`, the inspector's own offer.**
  - The spec declares no default. `language` is the discriminator of `HookBodySchema`: `z.literal('expression')` on one side and `z.literal('js', …)` on the other, with no `.default(…)` on either.
  - The inspector already offered `expression` in two places. It is the first entry of `BODY_LANG_OPTS`. It is also the value the Script language picker showed for a body that names no language: on `main` the picker's `value` reads `(typeof body.language === 'string' ? body.language : undefined) || 'expression'`.
  - It is now one constant, `SEEDED_BODY_LANGUAGE`, read by both the picker and the writer. The language the author sees selected is the language that is stored.
- **The switch into "Update fields" also writes the empty `patch` the spec requires.** On `main`, `commitOperation('update')` wrote no `patch`. The spec refused the result: "An `operation: 'update'` action has nothing to write". The switch now seeds `patch: {}` when the draft holds none. That is the skeleton Studio's New button starts from since objectui#11820, and `newActionPin` parses it. Any `patch` the draft already holds is kept.
- **An action that runs a registered function through `target`** gets no body seeded on the switch to *Run a script*. The spec accepts a `target` in place of a body.

Changeset: `.changeset/11921-script-action-language.md`, `patch` on `@object-ui/app-shell`. No export, prop, type member or language-pack key changes. Only an internal module of the inspector changes.

## Measurements behind the route (the dispatch hypotheses)

Every shape below was measured through the installed `@objectstack/spec` 17.7.0 `ActionSchema.safeParse` on the draft the inspector writes.

- **H1, the default exists: partly.** The spec has no declared default. The inspector's first option, and the value its picker shows when no language is named, is `expression`. Details above.
- **H2, one writer: confirmed and applied.** The paths that write a body are the switch, each keystroke, a language change, and a switch away and back. All of them now go through `writeScriptBody`. On `main`:
  - after the switch, the draft was refused at `body` ("A 'script' action requires either an inline `body` … or a `target`");
  - after the first keystroke, at `body.language` ("Invalid discriminator value. Expected 'expression' | 'js'");
  - after a language change from a JS body that carries `capabilities` to an expression, at `body` (`unrecognized_keys`). A JS body that has been through a parse always carries `capabilities`, because the spec defaults it to `[]`.
- **H3, nothing else changes: falsified for one write.** The Type control's write for every non-script type (`api`, `flow`, `modal`, `form`, `url`) is unchanged and writes no body. A control pins each one. The switch into an update action was not a parsing write, as measured above. It changes here under the bounded in-place exemption:
  - it is the same defect class, an operation switch that writes a shape the spec refuses;
  - the change is mechanical, and objectui#11820 already pins that exact shape;
  - no other claim holds this file;
  - the gate family is the same.

## Where the triage pin and the spec disagree

The triage pins "parse after the switch". Measured: a body that names only its language cannot parse in either language.

| Shape | Refusal |
|---|---|
| `body: { language }` | `body.source:invalid_type` |
| `body: { language, source: '' }` | `body.source:too_small` |

Both rows are true for `expression` and for `js`. `HookBodySchema` declares `source: z.string().min(1)` on both sides, so the switch can parse on its own only if a non-empty `source` (or a `target`) is written for the author. This PR does not write one. A seeded source would be a runnable handler the author never wrote, the no-op default class objectui#11820 removed. It would also have to be invented, and the dispatch rules out invented defaults.

So the pin is written as what the switch now guarantees:

- the body names the language the picker shows;
- the spec's **only** refusal is the missing `body.source`, the one input the editor puts in front of the author.

The last test of the first block measures the "why" rather than claiming it. The seat's call on this is raised in the dev report.

## Tests

All runs on `b3c799644`, the branch head (round 2: the key constant, the parity pin, and a merge of `main` `f3a0488`), from the worktree root, through `os-verify-lock.sh`. Round 1's numbers on `9bbaad1e7` are kept below where they still apply:

- New pin file `ActionDefaultInspector.scriptBodyLanguage-11921.test.tsx` (`scriptBodyPin`).
  - Command: `pnpm exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2 FILE`. Result: `Tests 13 passed (13)`, the 11 behaviour pins plus 2 parity pins (the same languages; per language, the same admitted keys).
  - What it does: it drives the real inspector in a host that merges each patch shallowly, the way the action hosts apply `onPatch`. It sends the held draft through a JSON round trip and parses it with `ActionSchema`.
  - Paths it pins: after the switch, after the first keystroke and while typing, after a language change both ways, a switch away and back, and a stored body with no language.
  - It also pins the JS-to-expression shape change, with a control for a key neither language admits, plus the three controls above.
- The 17 test files that name `ActionDefaultInspector` or `ObjectActionsPanel` (objectui#11820's `newActionPin` among them), plus `packages/core/src/utils/__tests__/column-identity.ratchet.test.ts`: `Test Files 18 passed (18)`, `Tests 154 passed (154)`.
- `pnpm --filter @object-ui/app-shell type-check` (`tsc --noEmit && tsc -p tsconfig.test.json`): exit 0. It ran after building the dependency closure (`turbo run build --filter='@object-ui/app-shell^...'`, 28 of 28 tasks successful). `tsc -p tsconfig.test.json --listFilesOnly` lists the new pin file.
- `pnpm exec eslint --format json` on the two changed `.ts`/`.tsx` files: 2 files judged, 0 errors, 0 warnings.
  - This is a narrowed run, and the narrowing is proven. The population is the `files: ['**/*.{ts,tsx}']` blocks of `eslint.config.js`. That config sets no `parserOptions.project` or `projectService`, so linting is not type-aware and this diff cannot move the verdict of any untouched file.
  - The repo-wide `pnpm lint` is CI's.
- Gates, each exit 0 with its own verdict line:
  - changeset gates: `scripts/check-changeset-{presence,no-major,overwrite,fixed}.mjs`, `check:changeset-claims`, `check:pending-changeset-literals`;
  - spec, metadata and action gates: `check:spec-symbols`, `check:metadata-write-doors`, `check:action-forward-parity`, `check:designer-field-key-parity`, `check:handler-key-reads`, `check:i18n-keys`;
  - citation and byte gates: `check:new-line-citations` ("0 new citation(s)"), `check:control-bytes`, `check:shell-escape-residue`;
  - dependency and import gates: `check:phantom-deps`, `check:self-import`, `check:esm-specifiers`, `check:unreferenced-sources`;
  - test-source gates: `check:test-path-roots`, `check:vi-mock-specifiers`, `check:vi-mock-inherit`, `check:vi-mock-override-shape`, `scripts/check-type-check-coverage.mjs`.

**Ablation.** Run with `node scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` from objectstack in WRAP mode on `9bbaad1e7`. The subject is imported from source by a relative path, so no `dist/` was involved.

- **Leg 1.** `writeScriptBody`'s `return next;` was replaced by the bare spread `return { ...body, ...change };` (anchor 1 to 0, blob `d9fe3748fba9` to `5720b777da8e`). Result: `Tests 5 failed | 6 passed (11)`, every failure an `AssertionError`. The failing tests were the switch, the first keystroke, away and back, the stored body with no language, and JS to expression. They fail with, for example, `expected { source: 'r' } to strictly equal { language: 'expression', source: 'r' }`.
- **Leg 2.** The update switch's `if (!hasPatch) cleared.patch = {};` was deleted (anchor 1 to 0, blob `d9fe3748fba9` to `4430ef259b01`). Result: `Tests 2 failed | 9 passed (11)`. The failing tests were away and back, refused at `patch:custom`, and the update-switch control.
- **Round 2, leg A.** A fake key `fakeKey` was added to the constant's `expression` entry (blob `7c2cfc2c03ae` to `36a8d8d8d988`). Result: `Tests 1 failed | 12 passed (13)`: the parity pin, with `expected [ 'fakeKey', 'language', 'source' ] to deeply equal [ 'language', 'source' ]`.
- **Round 2, leg B.** The spec key `timeoutMs` was removed from the `js` entry (blob `7c2cfc2c03ae` to `1916f10fa686`). Result: `Tests 2 failed | 11 passed (13)`: the parity pin and the JS-to-expression behaviour pin. The tool proved both restores (blob `7c2cfc2c03ae` equals HEAD).
- **Restore.** The tool proved the restore for both legs: blob after restore `d9fe3748fba9` equals the HEAD blob, and `git diff HEAD` is empty.

## Acceptance notes

Found on the way and not changed here. All three are reported to the seat with evidence.

- **The hook inspector has the same language-change write.** In `HookDefaultInspector.tsx`, `patchBody` is `{ ...body, ...p }`. Switching a JS hook body that carries `capabilities` to an expression writes a body that `HookSchema` refuses at `body` (`unrecognized_keys`). This was measured on `{ language: 'expression', source: 'return;', capabilities: ['api.read'] }`. New Studio hooks seed `{ language: 'js', source: 'return;' }`, so the missing-language half does not reach hooks created there.
- **The body editor's placeholder and hint are written for JS whatever language is picked.** The placeholder is `// (input, ctx) => result` then `return { ok: true }`. The hint is `engine.inspector.action.scriptBodyHint`, "Runs in the sandbox as (input, ctx) => Promise of output". The picker now stores Expression (L1) by default, the language it always showed. An author who types the placeholder's JS gets a body the spec parses as an expression. Whether lint or the runtime then refuses it was NOT MEASURED. The hook inspector already switches its placeholder by language; the action inspector would need a designer string, and `metadata-admin/i18n.ts` is outside this claim.
- **The Type control's switch to `script` still writes no body.** That draft is refused at `body` until the author types. With this PR the first keystroke now parses. A Type switch to `url`, `flow`, `modal`, `form` or `api` is refused at `target` until a target is set. That was measured on objectui#11820 and is unchanged here.

No doc sentence describes the script action's language. A `git grep` over `content/docs` and the app-shell README for the body language, "Run a script" and "Script language" found none; the same pipeline does match other `language` lines in `content/docs`.

**NOT MEASURED:**

- Browser verification in a running Studio. The pins drive the real inspector against the real spec.
- The rest of `@object-ui/app-shell`'s suite beyond the 18 files above. CI's `pnpm test` runs it.

**First-load bytes.** The first-round head's merge ref read 3307.6 KB against `main`'s 3307.0 KB. Round 2 removes the runtime spec import; CI's `Bundle Analysis` on this head is the measurement. Under ruling `6056819248` on objectui#11942, a byte-adding Studio fix lands against the 5 KB allowance once objectui#11937 has made `main` green.

Authored in session `https://claude.ai/code/session_01MgfduSkFrfM3eorB3UGfAU`. The seat is `domain:ui#2`, from claim comment 6055828336.
